assignmentHtml.task: Research Apache Flink as a stream-processing candidate. Investigate: (1) architecture — distributed stream processor with state backends; (2) ingestion — Kafka source with exactly-once, Debezium, JDBC; (3) updates/deletes — how Flink handles upserts (UpsertSink, JdbcSink), deduplication via keyed state; (4) joins — stream-stream, stream-table joins, CEP; (5) lake integration — Flink Iceberg catalog integration, time travel, compaction, cleaning; (6) recovery — savepoints/checkpoints, exactly-once semantics, what offsets/state are restored; (7) license — Apache 2.0; (8) version caveats. Position Flink: ingestion/transformation layer, not serving layer. Count as stateful component per accounting rule.
assignmentHtml.context: Evidence cutoff 2026-09-16. Open-source analytics platform investigation. Flink is a candidate in ingestion/transformation layer. The 3-stateful-component limit matters. Flink checkpoint lifecycle counts as a stateful component. Need to know exactly what Flink recovers and when.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: Structured dossier for Apache Flink covering architecture, ingestion/CDC, updates/dedup, joins, lake integration, recovery, license, version caveats, with source URLs.

answerHtml: Apache Flink is a distributed stream-processing engine positioned as an ingestion/transformation layer (not a serving layer). It is a stateful component: keyed/operator state persists across events and is snapshotted via checkpoints, each of which constitutes a stateful component per accounting rules. Below is a structured dossier covering all eight dimensions.

evidence.snippet: Flink is a framework and distributed processing engine for stateful computations over unbounded and bounded data streams. Keyed state is partitioned and distributed strictly together with the streams; organized into key groups (atomic redistribution units). State backends: HashMapStateBackend (in-memory hash map) and RocksDB-based backend. Fault tolerance via stream replay + checkpointing: a checkpoint marks a specific point in each input stream along with corresponding operator state, enabling exactly-once resumption.
evidence.supports: Architecture: distributed DAG-based stream processor with pluggable state backends; state partitioned with data streams

evidence.snippet: HashMapStateBackend holds data as objects on JVM heap (fast, memory-limited). EmbeddedRocksDBStateBackend stores serialized byte arrays on local disk (scales with disk, ~10x slower, only backend supporting incremental checkpoints, async snapshots). Config via state.backend.type (hashmap/rocksdb/forst).
evidence.supports: State backends: HashMap (heap/performance), RocksDB (disk/scalability), ForSt (new in 2.0, disaggregated)

evidence.snippet: Flink CDC sources ingest database changes via CDC; some integrate Debezium as the engine. Supports mysql-cdc, postgres-cdc, oracle-cdc, sqlserver-cdc, mongodb-cdc, tidb-cdc, db2-cdc, vitess-cdc, oceanbase-cdc. Features: exactly-once processing, parallel read, incremental snapshot read. DataStream API connectors consume changes without requiring Debezium or Kafka deployed separately.
evidence.supports: Ingestion: native JDBC-based CDC sources (no Kafka intermediary needed), Debezium integration, exactly-once guarantees for most connectors

evidence.snippet: Flink interprets Debezium JSON/Avro messages as INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE messages. Debezium delivers exactly-once under normal operation but falls to at-least-once during failover. Flink config table.exec.source.cdc-events-duplicate=true plus PRIMARY KEY generates an additional stateful deduplication operator. Flink encodes UPDATE_BEFORE/UPDATE_AFTER as separate DELETE/INSERT Debezium messages.
evidence.supports: Debezium format support in Flink SQL; duplicate-event handling via stateful dedup keyed on primary key

evidence.snippet: Kafka source commits offsets when checkpoints complete (for monitoring/progress exposure, not fault tolerance — Flink uses checkpoint state, not committed offsets, for recovery). KafkaSink EXACTLY_ONCE mode writes messages in a Kafka transaction committed on checkpoint; requires setTransactionalIdPrefix and unique prefix per app; delays visibility until checkpoint commit. AT_LEAST_ONCE waits for producer acks on checkpoint.
evidence.supports: Kafka source/sink exactly-once mechanics: offsets restored from checkpoints, sink transactions committed at checkpoint barrier

evidence.snippet: Debezium provides at-least-once delivery by default. Exactly-once requires Kafka Connect's EOS support (KIP-618): Kafka Connect 3.3.0+, workers set exactly.once.source.support=enabled, connector set exactly.once.support=required. Supported: MariaDB, MongoDB, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server. Known open Kafka JIRA issues may affect correctness in edge cases.
evidence.supports: Debezium Kafka Connect EOS requires Kafka Connect 3.3+; Flink CDC handles duplicates internally instead

evidence.snippet: JDBC sink operates in upsert mode if a primary key is defined in DDL; otherwise append mode. In upsert mode, Flink atomically inserts new rows or updates existing rows via DB-specific DML (MySQL: INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE; PostgreSQL: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET; Oracle/SQL Server: MERGE INTO). Provides idempotence for failure recovery re-processing.
evidence.supports: JdbcSink upsert semantics tied to DDL primary key; idempotent writes enable dedup on recovery

evidence.snippet: Upsert Kafka sink consumes changelog; writes INSERT/UPDATE_AFTER as normal messages, DELETE as tombstones (null values). Partitions by primary key so same-key updates land in same partition. Buffer-flush retains last record per key (sink.buffer-flush.max-rows + interval must both be >0). Default at-least-once; exactly-once via Kafka transactions with checkpointing. Last record per key takes effect when read back, giving idempotent writes like HBase sink.
evidence.supports: UpsertKafka deduplication by key via buffering; idempotent semantics; exactly-once with transactions

evidence.snippet: Deduplication removes rows duplicating over a set of columns using ROW_NUMBER() (a special case of Top-N where N=1, ordered by processing or event time). Required exact syntax: QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY col1... ORDER BY time_attr [asc|desc]) = 1. ASC keeps first row, DESC keeps last. PARTITION BY columns serve as the dedup key (implicitly keyed state).
evidence.supports: SQL-level dedup via ROW_NUMBER() with strict syntax; preserves first or last occurrence per dedup key

evidence.snippet: Keyed state (MapState/ValueState/ListState) is used in KeyedProcessFunction for per-key deduplication: check if key seen; if not, store and optionally register timer; on timer fire, emit and clear state. State TTL recommended to purge old entries and prevent memory bloat.
evidence.supports: DataStream API dedup via keyed state + timers; best practice includes state TTL

evidence.snippet: Regular joins: any new record affects entire join result; requires keeping both sides in Flink state forever (unbounded growth unless TTL configured). Interval joins: Cartesian product restricted by time constraint and equi-predicate; only append-only tables with time attributes (state can be pruned). Temporal joins (event-time FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF retrieves key value at past point; processing-time returns latest version, used for dimension enrichment). Lookup joins: processing-time temporal join against external lookup source connector (e.g., JDBC).
evidence.supports: Stream-stream (regular/interval), stream-table (temporal/lookup), CEP via pattern contiguity

evidence.snippet: FlinkCEP detects event patterns in endless streams. Pattern API with quantifiers (oneOrMore, times, optional, greedy) and conditions (where, or, until, subtype). Contiguity between patterns: strict next(), relaxed followedBy(), non-deterministic relaxed followedByAny(). Matches emitted via PatternProcessFunction receiving Map<String, List<IN>>. Late events buffered and sorted by timestamp in event time. AfterMatchSkipStrategy controls duplicate match emission.
evidence.supports: CEP library for pattern detection; contiguity conditions act as join semantics over event sequences

evidence.snippet: TableMaintenance API empowers Flink jobs to execute maintenance natively in streaming or batch mode: ExpireSnapshots (removes old snapshots/files, maxSnapshotAge, retainLast), RewriteDataFiles (compacts small files, targetFileSizeBytes, partial progress), DeleteOrphanFiles (removes unreferenced files, minAge). Can be scheduled by commit count, data file count, or time interval; or embedded in IcebergSink V2 via addPostCommitTopology and SQL SET commands (table.exec.iceberg.use-v2-sink + flink-maintenance.*).
evidence.supports: Lake integration: compaction, snapshot expiration, orphan cleanup — all executable inside Flink jobs, with post-commit triggers

evidence.snippet: Flink Iceberg read options for time travel: snapshot-id (batch: read specified snapshot), as-of-timestamp (batch: most recent snapshot as of given ms), start-snapshot-id/end-snapshot-id, start-tag/end-tag, branch, starting-strategy (streaming: INCREMENTAL_FROM_LATEST_SNAPSHOT default, INCREMENTAL_FROM_EARLIEST_SNAPSHOT, INCREMENTAL_FROM_SNAPSHOT_ID, INCREMENTAL_FROM_SNAPSHOT_TIMESTAMP). Read option > Flink config > table property priority.
evidence.supports: Time travel via snapshot-id/as-of-timestamp options; streaming starting strategies for incremental reads from historical points

evidence.snippet: Checkpointing requires durable replayable source (Kafka, etc.) and durable state storage (HDFS/S3). Mode: EXACTLY_ONCE (default) vs AT_LEAST_ONCE. Checkpoints store consistent snapshots of all state including timers, stateful operators, connectors, windows, user-defined state. UnionListState used for global offset views (e.g., Kafka partition offsets) gets special handling. Externalized checkpoints persist metadata beyond job lifetime. num-retained configurable.
evidence.supports: What's restored: full operator state + source positions/offsets; checkpoint storage options; externalized checkpoint retention

evidence.snippet: Checkpoint = automatic snapshot for fault recovery (can be incremental); Savepoint = manual snapshot for operational purposes (always complete, optimized for flexibility). Asynchronous barrier snapshotting (Chandy-Lamport variant): sources record offsets, insert barriers; operators record state; two-input operators align barriers. Exactly-once end-to-end requires replayable sources + transactional/idempotent sinks. State backends use copy-on-write for async snapshots. Only EmbeddedRocksDB supports incremental snapshots.
evidence.supports: Recovery: what happens on failure (restore state + rewind/replay from checkpointed offsets); savepoint vs checkpoint distinction

evidence.snippet: A checkpoint is a consistent snapshot of application state AND input stream position. On failure, Flink resumes from most recent completed checkpoint, restoring state and rolling back to correct input position. End-to-end exactly-once requires external systems supporting two-phase commit: Kafka sink pre-commits transaction in pre-commit phase, commits in commit phase after JobManager issues checkpoint-completed callbacks. TwoPhaseCommitSinkFunction encapsulates this.
evidence.supports: End-to-end exactly-once mechanics: barrier alignment, two-phase commit for sink transactions, offsets restored from checkpoint

evidence.snippet: Apache Flink® 2.3.0 is the latest stable release (released 2026-06-25). Flink CDC 3.6 is the latest stable release. EOL policy: support current + previous minor release with bugfixes; one final patch release for the version losing support. All releases under Apache License 2.0 (ASF project).
evidence.supports: License: Apache 2.0; current version 2.3.0; support/EOL policy

evidence.snippet: Flink 2.0 breaking changes: DataSet API removed; Scala API removed; Java 8 unsupported (minimum Java 11, recommended 17, supports 21); legacy flink-conf.yaml replaced with config.yaml; state compatibility NOT guaranteed between 1.x and 2.x; per-job deployment mode removed (use Application mode). New: Disaggregated State Management with DFS, ForSt state backend, Materialized Tables, Adaptive Batch Execution, Paimon streaming lakehouse integration.
evidence.supports: Version caveats: major breaking changes in 2.0, especially state compatibility break between 1.x and 2.x

evidence.snippet: Flink 2.3.0: FROM_CHANGELOG/TO_CHANGELOG table functions; materialized table DDL parity; SinkUpsertMaterializer now FAILS AT PLANNING TIME when upsert key differs from primary key unless explicit ON CONFLICT clause (DO NOTHING/DO ERROR/DO DEDUPLICATE); mini-batch aggregation record-loss bug fixed; native S3 filesystem (experimental); watermark alignment buffer redesigned; checkpointing during recovery opt-in; application lifecycle management. Upgrade notes required for SinkUpsertMaterializer behavior.
evidence.supports: Version caveats for 2.3: SinkUpsertMaterializer behavior change breaks queries with differing upsert/primary keys; new experimental features
